How USB-C won the decades-long cable standards war
recent_posts.summary: USB-C has effectively won the decades-long cable standards war, accelerated by the EU mandating its adoption across consumer electronics including laptops. While USB-C looks simple, it hides significant complexity — not every cable supports the same features, and the ecosystem still relies on certification and controller chips. The EU's regulatory push is credited with forcing holdouts like Apple to abandon proprietary connectors, reducing e-waste and simplifying the consumer experience.

recent_posts.title: How OpenAI’s weird corporate structure became a lawsuit
recent_posts.summary: OpenAI's unusual hybrid corporate structure — a nonprofit parent controlling a for-profit arm — is at the center of Elon Musk's lawsuit against the company. Musk claims OpenAI abandoned its founding mission to build AGI for humanity's benefit, while OpenAI argues a commercial structure was always necessary and that Musk is attacking a competitor. With Microsoft having poured billions into the company, the case raises a fundamental question: can a nonprofit-originated AI company claim to serve humanity while running one of the world's most valuable startups?

recent_posts.title: Leaked pitch deck reveals how ChatGPT ads will work using prompt relevance targeting
recent_posts.summary: A leaked pitch deck from ad platform StackAdapt reveals how advertising inside ChatGPT will work. Ads will be priced between $15–$60 CPM with a $50,000 minimum spend for the pilot program. Rather than third-party cookies, targeting will be based on 'prompt relevance' — the system reads the semantic intent of user queries in real time and serves contextually matched ads. This model closely resembles how Google's search ads work and represents a significant threat to Google's dominance, while also marking a broader shift from identity-based to intent-based advertising.

top_posts.title: Instagram put Reels on TV because TV ads pay more
top_posts.summary: Instagram is launching Reels on Amazon Fire TV, primarily to capitalize on higher advertising rates. TV screen ads command up to three times more revenue than mobile ads for identical content. With YouTube already generating over a billion hours of daily watch time on televisions, Instagram is strategically moving short-form video content from mobile devices to living rooms where premium advertising dollars are concentrated.

top_posts.title: The FTC quietly removed key AI guidance
top_posts.summary: The FTC has quietly removed multiple blog posts about AI from its website without explanation. The deleted content covered topics like open-source AI risks and dangers of rushing AI tools to market. While not legally binding, these posts helped companies understand regulatory thinking and enforcement priorities. The removal makes it harder to track how the FTC's AI policy stance is evolving and effectively erases part of the public record, leaving businesses uncertain about which guidance still applies.

top_posts.title: Stores now have to tell you when prices are personalized
top_posts.summary: New York passed a law requiring retailers to disclose when they use algorithmic pricing based on personal data like browsing history, location, or purchase patterns. However, stores only need to display a notice about personalized pricing without revealing whether customers pay more or less than others, or explaining the pricing formula. The law creates compliance challenges for retailers who must build audit systems, track consents, and ensure third-party vendor compliance, while providing limited transparency to consumers.

top_posts.title: Lawyers fined for submitting AI-hallucinated fake court cases
top_posts.summary: Over 800 lawyers have faced legal consequences, including $110,000 in fines in Oregon, for submitting AI-generated court documents containing fabricated legal precedents. The root cause is a fundamental misunderstanding of how LLMs work: unlike search engines that retrieve existing facts, LLMs are probabilistic text generators that predict likely word sequences. When asked for legal citations, they generate convincing but entirely fictional case names, rulings, and citation numbers. AI is useful for summarizing existing content but unreliable as a factual lookup tool.

top_posts.title: Anthropic source code leak exposed Claude Code architecture and unreleased features
top_posts.summary: A security researcher discovered that Anthropic accidentally included a source map file in Claude Code's public npm package, exposing over 500,000 lines of TypeScript source code across nearly 1,900 files. The leaked code revealed Claude's full tool architecture, an undocumented internal memory system with a 200-line cap, a silent model downgrade from Opus to Sonnet after server errors, unreleased features with internal codenames (including a persistent background agent called 'Chairos mode' and an 'Ultra plan'), and internal model names. Anthropic attributed the leak to human error via a default build tool setting, noting no customer data was exposed. However, the architectural blueprints spread rapidly on GitHub, prompting over 8,000 DMCA takedowns. Developers circumvented these by using AI to rewrite the code in other languages, meaning the information is effectively public.
